title: Zhu
capsule: Zhu (邾) was a small Zhou-dynasty vassal state in southwestern Shandong, traditionally founded c. 1046 BCE as a fief of the Cao clan holding the rank of viscount under the Zhou kings. A regular though minor participant in the interstate covenants recorded in the Zuo Zhuan, the state was later renamed Zou (鄒) around 417–377 BCE during the reign of Duke Mu of Lu. It achieved cultural renown as the birthplace of the philosopher Mencius (c. 372–289 BCE), but militarily could not resist its larger neighbors; the state of Chu under King Xuan (r. 369–340 BCE) conquered and absorbed it, ending its independent existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Zhu/Zou appears in classical Chinese annals (Zuo Zhuan, Shiji) with reasonable political detail, but its territorial extent is poorly defined and reconstructed from sparse textual references without archaeological boundary evidence.
